scope: An independent optical calibration and subsequent fresh dose validation. Specified while the original lever trials were in progress. The originally frozen two-scale forecasts and their failure criteria remain in the record.
question: Does a transfer measured on clear glass give a reproducible nominal volume when its calibration is taken directly from photographed graduation crossings?
optical_calibration: Move the cup level past the front-wall three-quarter, one and one-and-a-quarter US-cup graduation tips. Use small bounded pulses and stationary photographs on both sides of each crossing in both directions. Locate the printed cap and the contact in unprinted glass beside it; solve the sign change as a function of the separately observed liquid row at x990. The number, width, or speed of the pump pulses is never a volume reference. Preserve the crossing brackets and uncertainty.
optical_checks: Use the lowering direction to fit a monotone piecewise-linear map with the three known graduation volumes. Predict the volumes at the independently photographed rising-direction crossings. Require absolute error <=1.5 mL at each of the three anchors to call the scale repeatable across direction. Compare the separately printed right and left one-cup contact as an independent parallax check; report both if they differ. Report the middle-anchor residual when interpolating only the outer anchors. No absolute glass or external gravimetric accuracy is claimed.
flow_validation: After the optical map is frozen, convert original calibration endpoints to nominal mL with that map, fit the same four head-specific per-burst medians and sum interpolations for fresh held-out pour schedules. Freeze forecasts before the new pours. For each tested scenario and head require at least five of six within max(1 mL, 10% of forecast) and absolute mean bias <= max(0.6 mL, 5%). Compare on a distinct camera sightline when calibrated. Report actual completion, every miss and limits.
idle_hypothesis: With both pumps off from five through sixty-five seconds after reaching each extreme cup level, apparent net transfer stays within 0.75 nominal mL at both ends. Take early, intermediate and late exposures and compare native direction/displacement to optical variability. Movement or failure of either independent reading to resolve the limit leaves the hypothesis unconfirmed.
restoration: Return to the initial stationary cup reference, restore the detected channel selection and stored channel ratios, confirm state and valves, close the camera and restore its original settings.
